title: pvExtractCellsByRegion
body:
## pvExtractCellsByRegion

Extracts the cells lying entirely inside (ParaView default) or entirely outside an implicit region — a Plane (ParaView's default choice, whose inside is the side opposite its normal), Box or Sphere — without cutting them, and outputs an unstructured grid. Extractintersected adds cells straddling the region boundary and Extractonlyintersected keeps only those. Use it to cut out a sub-volume of whole original cells; clip cuts cells exactly at the surface and slice returns the surface itself.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The cut is jagged because whole cells are kept; use clip for an exact boundary.
- For a Plane, inside is the negative side, opposite to the normal; flip the normal or choose outside to keep the other half.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ExtractCellsByRegion`. Identity: `filters/ExtractGeometry`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Slice filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Extractintersected` | This parameter controls whether to extract cells that are on the boundary of the region. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ExtractionSide` | This parameter controls whether to extract cells that are inside or outside the region. | `{"type":"enum","values":["outside","inside"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"outside"` |
| `Extractonlyintersected` | This parameter controls whether to extract only cells that are on the boundary of the region. If this parameter is set, the Extraction Side parameter is ignored. If Extract Intersected is off, this parameter has no effect. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `IntersectWith` | This property sets the region used to extract cells. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Box","Plane","Sphere"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Box"}` |

### Nested `IntersectWith` → `Box`

Syntax: `{"type":"Box","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Box`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IntersectWith.options.Bounds` | Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Length` | With UseReferenceBounds false: edge lengths [Lx, Ly, Lz] of the box along its own axes (ParaView applies them as scale factors to a unit cube). With UseReferenceBounds true: dimensionless scale factors applied to the Bounds box about the coordinate origin. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Position` | With UseReferenceBounds false: world coordinates [x, y, z] of the box’s minimum corner (before rotation); the box extends from Position to Position + Length along its own axes. With UseReferenceBounds true: a translation applied to the transformed Bounds box. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Rotation` | Rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] about the x, y and z axes, applied about the box’s local origin (its minimum corner at Position, not its centre; with UseReferenceBounds true, about the coordinate origin). The angles are combined in VTK’s Z-X-Y convention: the box transform is Translate · RotateZ · RotateX · RotateY · Scale. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.UseReferenceBounds` | Chooses how the box is defined. False: the box is a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated about its corner and placed at Position. True: the box starts from Bounds, and Length, Rotation and Position act as scale, rotation and translation relative to it (about the coordinate origin). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `IntersectWith` → `Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IntersectWith.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `IntersectWith` → `Sphere`

Syntax: `{"type":"Sphere","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Sphere`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IntersectWith.options.Center` | Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere in the input’s coordinates; the region within Radius of this point is inside. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `IntersectWith.options.Radius` | Radius of the sphere: points closer than Radius to Center are inside. A larger radius encloses more of the data or moves the cut shell outward. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
